verdict.rationale: Recurly documents subscription plan changes with control over credits and proration, credit invoices with an audit trail and webhooks, and an API with official client libraries in seven languages, so an agent could perform these operations programmatically. The Compass MCP server is described as letting agents such as Claude Desktop or Cursor work with Recurly's tools and APIs, but it is also framed as connecting tools to documentation and API knowledge, so its ability to take billing actions is unclear. Missing for 10: any evidence of scoped or restricted API key permissions for agents, explicit documentation of API endpoints for creating subscriptions and applying credits, clarity that the MCP server can perform write operations, and independent hands-on corroboration.
